chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Anṣārī, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Abī ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in a free Muslim woman praying while her head is uncovered.

key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head; the body part mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الْحُرَّةِ: free; distinguishing her legal status from a bondwoman
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman; the female subject addressed in the ruling
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمَةِ: the Muslim woman; specifying the woman as belonging to Islam
key_terms.تُصَلِّيَ: to perform salat; to pray ritually
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a free Muslim woman to perform salat with her head uncovered?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling concerning the validity or permissibility of salat for a free Muslim woman praying with her head uncovered. It belongs to the jurisprudential discussion of what clothing is permissible in prayer.
